properties.areaDesc: Anne Arundel
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 5 at 8:45AM EST until November 5 at 6:00PM EST by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low lying areas due to tidal flooding.

* WHERE...Shoreline in Anne Arundel County.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM EST this evening, especially around the time
of high tide.

* IMPACTS...At 2.6 feet, water may begin to pond in the parking
lot at Annapolis City Dock, and surround the Alex Haley
Memorial.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides one to one and a half feet above
normal. High tide at Annapolis U.S. Naval Academy is at 2:30 PM.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 6 PM EST THIS EVENING

properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...North Central Socorro County in central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River or stream flows are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 500 PM MST, emergency management reported flooding in the
advisory area from rising river levels along the Rio Puerco. This
will cause arroyo and small stream flooding. Rapid river rises
will cause minor flooding in the advisory area.
- For Rio Puerco at Bernardo:
At 4:00pm the stage was 14.08 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.5 feet.
- For Rio Grande at San Acacia:
At 4:45pm the stage was 14.83 feet.
Flood Stage is 23.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 4 at 3:29PM PST until November 5 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 11 ft with dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional High Surf Advisories and Coastal
Flood Advisories may be needed in the near future.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.
